rules.title: Wildcard and ref-binding patterns are irrefutable
rules.statement: A wildcard pattern `_`/binder and a `ref`-binding pattern impose no match constraint (their refutability test is always true).

rules.title: Integer/bool literal patterns test value equality
rules.statement: An integer or bool literal pattern matches iff the scrutinee value loaded at the scrutinee's type equals the literal (bool encoded 1/0); the literal constant is coerced to the scrutinee's element type before comparison.

rules.title: Range pattern tests inclusive low<=v<=high
rules.statement: A range pattern matches iff lo <= v <= hi (both bounds inclusive). The comparison is unsigned when the scrutinee type is one of {u8,u16,u32,u64,usize,char,bool}, signed otherwise.

rules.title: Tuple pattern matches by conjunction of element tests
rules.statement: A tuple pattern matches iff every sub-pattern matches its corresponding element (positional, by index); the overall test is the conjunction of element tests. Element addresses are taken in place; a tuple value is stored inline (the scrutinee place IS the tuple storage, no extra load).

rules.title: Enum variant pattern tests discriminant equality only
rules.statement: A variant pattern (with or without payload) matches iff the scrutinee enum's discriminant equals the variant's discriminant (an i32 compare). Payload sub-patterns contribute only bindings; refutable inner sub-patterns are checked separately via the match guard channel, not by this test.

rules.title: C-like (all-nullary) enum value is its discriminant
rules.statement: An enum with no tagged payload (all-nullary) is represented as a bare i32 discriminant with no heap/struct storage; a variant pattern on it loads that i32 and compares to the variant discriminant.

rules.title: Variant test through references peels every reference layer
rules.statement: When the scrutinee type is `&`/`&mut` (to arbitrary depth) wrapping an enum, the discriminant test dereferences once per reference layer to reach the inline enum storage before reading the discriminant; the tagged-enum spec is resolved off the underlying enum type, not the reference wrapper.

rules.title: Or-pattern matches if any alternative matches
rules.statement: An or-pattern `P1 | P2 | ...` matches iff at least one alternative matches; the test is the disjunction of the alternatives' tests, each evaluated against the same scrutinee place and type.

rules.title: Struct pattern matches by conjunction of refutable field tests
rules.statement: A struct pattern matches iff every refutable named-field sub-pattern matches its field; the test is the conjunction over fields. Irrefutable field subs (bind / shorthand / wildcard / ref-bind) contribute no constraint. The scrutinee place IS the struct storage; each field is GEP'd by name.

rules.title: Reference pattern `&P` dereferences then tests inner
rules.statement: A reference pattern `&P` / `&mut P` against a reference-typed scrutinee loads the reference (the pointed-to address) and tests P against the pointee type; against a non-reference scrutinee the inner is tested in place.

rules.title: At-binding `name @ P` is the refutability of P
rules.statement: An at-binding pattern `name @ P` is irrefutable in its binding part; its match constraint is exactly the refutability test of the sub-pattern P.

rules.title: Fixed-array slice pattern: no length gate, positional prefix/suffix tests
rules.statement: A slice pattern against a `[T;N]` array (or reference to one) has fixed length, so it imposes no length check; it tests prefix sub-patterns at indices 0.. and suffix sub-patterns at indices N-suffix_count.. , conjoining all non-wildcard sub-tests.

rules.title: Dynamic slice pattern gates on length then tests elements
rules.statement: A slice pattern against a dynamic `&[T]` first compares the runtime length: with a rest binding `..` the slice must have length >= prefix_count+suffix_count, otherwise exactly == prefix_count+suffix_count; on success prefix elements are tested positionally against the data pointer. This length comparison is conjoined with element sub-tests.

rules.title: Aggregate binding binds the place; scalar binding copies
rules.statement: Binding a name to a struct/zoned-struct/tuple value binds the storage address (place) without copying; binding a name to a scalar loads the value and stores it into a fresh local. Struct bindings additionally record the bound place's struct shape so field access GEPs through it.

rules.title: Slice/closure/trait-object binding binds the fat-pointer place
rules.statement: Binding a name to a slice, closure, or trait-object value (a 16-byte inline fat pair) binds the storage pointer (stored into a pointer-typed local), so the value convention is uniform with a pointer-valued scalar.

rules.title: Tuple binding binds each element, dereferencing a reference scrutinee
rules.statement: A tuple pattern binds each sub-pattern to the corresponding element (by index); a `&(T,U)`/`&mut (T,U)` scrutinee is dereferenced to obtain element types before binding.

rules.title: Variant payload binding dereferences reference layers then binds payload
rules.statement: Binding a variant-data pattern dereferences every `&`/`&mut` layer (e.g. `&&Option<T>` binds payload as `&&T`) to reach the inline enum storage, resolves the tagged-enum spec off the underlying enum type, then binds the variant's payload sub-patterns.

rules.title: Or-pattern bindings share one storage per name across alternatives
rules.statement: An or-pattern's alternatives bind the same set of names with the same types; one shared local is allocated per bound name and each alternative binds into the shared local, so the join point observes a single storage per name.

rules.title: Struct pattern binding: shorthand binds field by its name
rules.statement: A struct pattern binds each named field; field shorthand `{x}` binds the field value to `x` (aggregate fields bind the place, scalar fields copy), `{x: a}` rebinds via the sub-pattern, and refutable subs bind their inner names.

rules.title: `ref x` binds a borrow (the address), not a copy
rules.statement: A `ref x` binding (and default-binding-mode ref) binds `x : &T` to the scrutinee place's address without loading or copying; a ref-to-struct binds the pointer and records struct shape for field access, a scalar ref alloca-wraps the address so `*x` derefs one level.

rules.title: Diverging match scrutinee makes arms dead code
rules.statement: If a match's scrutinee diverges (e.g. `match return x { ... }`), evaluation of the scrutinee terminates control flow and the arms are unreachable.
